# routeur_workspace_model (Resource)

Whether a workspace routes to one upstream model. Models are opt-in per workspace: declaring this resource activates the model, and destroying it deactivates it again (models themselves are never created or deleted). A provider's models are listed once the organisation has an enabled `routeur_provider_credential` for it; the `routeur_workspace_models` data source lists them. Build `model` from the credential's `provider_name` (`"${routeur_provider_credential.openai.provider_name}:gpt-4o"`) and Terraform creates the credential first and removes it last, with no `depends_on`.

The API refuses to deactivate a model that a routing rule in the workspace pins or lists as a failover target (error `model_in_use`, naming the rules), whether that rule is enabled or not. Reference this resource's `provider_name` and `model_id` from those rules: Terraform then changes or removes the rules before it deactivates the model.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "routeur_provider_credential" "openai" {
  provider_name = "openai"
  label         = "prod"
  key           = var.openai_api_key
}

data "routeur_workspace" "default" {
  slug = "default"
}

# Route the default workspace to two OpenAI models. Destroying a resource
# deactivates its model again.
resource "routeur_workspace_model" "openai" {
  for_each = toset(["gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini"])

  workspace_id = data.routeur_workspace.default.id
  # Referencing the credential creates it before the models need it.
  model = "${routeur_provider_credential.openai.provider_name}:${each.key}"
}

variable "openai_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `model` (String) The model, as `<provider>:<model_id>`, e.g. `openai:gpt-4o` (model ids may contain `/` and `:`, as some fine-tuned and discovered models do). Changing it replaces the resource.
- `workspace_id` (String) Id of the workspace this belongs to (`ws_…`), e.g. `routeur_workspace.example.id`. The `routeur_workspace` data source resolves a slug to its id. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the workspace routes to the model. Defaults to `true`; set `false` to keep the model managed but deactivated. Deactivating a model a routing rule still uses is refused (`model_in_use`).

### Read-Only

- `availability` (String) Last provider discovery result: `available`, `unavailable` or `deprecated`; null if never observed. New values may be added.
- `capabilities` (Set of String) Capabilities from the curated catalogue, e.g. `text`, `tools` (a set: order carries no meaning); empty when uncatalogued.
- `catalogued` (Boolean) False for a model discovered at the provider but not yet in routeur.ai's curated catalogue (prices and context may then be null).
- `context_tokens` (Number) Context window in tokens; null when unknown.
- `display_name` (String) Curated name; the model id when uncatalogued.
- `id` (String) `<workspace_id>/<model>`, e.g. `ws_3/openai:gpt-4o`.
- `input_per_1k` (Number) Input price per 1,000 tokens, in USD; null when unknown.
- `model_id` (String) The upstream model id. May contain `/` or `:`.
- `output_per_1k` (Number) Output price per 1,000 tokens, in USD; null when unknown.
- `provider_name` (String) Provider slug, e.g. `openai`. (The API calls this field `provider`, a name Terraform reserves.)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# id: <workspace_id>/<provider>:<model_id>; the model id may itself
# contain "/".
import {
  to = routeur_workspace_model.openai["gpt-4o"]
  id = "ws_3/openai:gpt-4o"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <workspace_id>/<provider>:<model_id>; the model id may itself contain "/".
terraform import 'routeur_workspace_model.openai["gpt-4o"]' ws_3/openai:gpt-4o
terraform import 'routeur_workspace_model.openai["ft/custom-model"]' ws_3/openai:ft/custom-model
```
